author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Shakespeare's actors made reputation depend on what an audience heard and believed. This comedy gives overheard conversations the power to arrange love or destroy a person's standing.

hook.text: How easily could someone talk you out of trusting a good person?

paragraphs: Beatrice and Benedick know how to make a conversation into a contest. Neither intends to surrender the last word. Around them, other people have begun making plans for who should love whom.

The comedy delights in the possibility that a little deception can help someone recognise a feeling. Then it places that possibility beside a much darker use of the same technique. What we think we have witnessed may already have been staged for us.

Shakespeare connects wit with trust. A person who can answer every insult may still struggle to say something vulnerable. A person eager to believe an accusation may call that eagerness honour. The costs fall unevenly, especially when a woman's reputation is treated as public property.
Enjoy the verbal fencing, but listen for the point at which being clever is no longer enough. What would you be willing to risk to stand beside someone everyone else had decided to condemn?

orientation.text: The Beatrice–Benedick relationship develops alongside Hero and Claudio's. Overhearing connects the plots, but the intentions and consequences differ.
